newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Building sector boosts Senegal's economy.
newsitem.headline: Building sector boosts Senegal's economy.

text.p: Senegal's president, Abdou Diouf, said on Wednesday the building sector had boosted his country's growth to 5.2 percent in 1996.

"The rate of growth of the Gross Domestic Product reached 5.2 percent in 1996. It is in steady progress since 1994. Many sectors has contributed, in particular, the building sector," Diouf told Senegal's Economic and Social Council.
Senegal's GDP was 4.8 percent in 1995 and inflation at the end of 1996 was three percent. The projection for 1997 was an inflation of 2.5 percent.
The building sector has benefited mainly from money being repatriated by Senegalese leaving abroad. Their income in local currency terms almost doubled after the devaluation of CFA franc in 1994.
With demand for cement growing, officials at the country's sole cement factory have said it will double its production from 813,000 tonnes per year to 1,500,000 over the next 21 months.
Senegalese Economy Minister Papa Ousmane Sacko has acknowledged that there is a market for a second and even a third cement factory in the country.
Diouf said the government was working hard to cut the budget deficit. "Tough management of public finance led to the reduction of the budget deficit," he added.
Senegal aims to eliminate its budget deficit -- it was 1.9 percent of GDP in 1996 -- and turn it into a surplus if one percent of GDP in 1999.
